feedback_interpretation: H_nitrogen is strengthened but remains graph-specific. Observed e47aebe2660b9e1528de measured m216 at 10/1 as 53.42/92.93 mL, rejecting its historical decline. Observed 4659b6752f23c0b85f08 and 49201b5817f204116f7f measured m66 completions of 55.06 and 119.31 mL at 2/1 and 5/1, demonstrating failed transfer after quinoline supervision; historical V2 underprediction reached 92.12 mL. Accurate 2feb7d8e0a3566ddf97f and moderate aminoester retention in 70593725787c65a74951 oppose a blanket nitrogen correction. H_OH gains support from the differentiated alcohol measurements and the m99 rise from 6.47/13.36 to 19.91/32.37 mL in 36786ca0d1deaa0687ba and 12ab195583f05b9aa177. H_shape is refined: 61090cfdcf019e0891a3 confirms m82's 20/1 rise, and 93f10a8edf06f7acae26 rejects m91's predicted collapsed interval. The smaller pure-EA errors in 3554059c7f0676bb2e03 oppose a persistent sulfoxide offset. Conversely, 4a39c1f64d17e050e4a5 and 39815ababe97d7acc107 record decreasing m194 completion from 1/1 to 5/1, preventing a universal solvent-monotonicity correction. H_m73 is weakened: near-repeat 45dca237351265a8f169 measured 4.89/10.59 versus 18.60/18.96 mL in 2cf789c87f7c6325c020. The 0.01 mg difference does not establish a loading explanation, and the m165 pair also weakens transfer of the proposed maximum. Neither conflicting m73 record is identified as erroneous. Observed aa65e86ee8638bded5d9 and 40fd02db79e028fe05a9 reject m80's predicted intermediate completion maximum, reducing the value of further weak-eluent sampling there. Observed 65fcce0299e031dedeb8 confirms late m173 completion with the smaller plug, at 78.37 mL. Its approximately 30.53 mL plug-associated difference at 1/1 contrasts with 1.16 mL at 2/1, motivating a localized interaction question without establishing causality. The m92 2/1 contrast in 10a4c811b70ba8155044 and f7cc49c21fea55ed9087 moves onset and completion later by 0.51 and 0.83 mL, widening the interval by only 0.32 mL; conditional loading responses remain supported without establishing significance or smoothness. The m9 comparison c45a62392f6a5694efe6 and e515cb1302d9dac0b8cd gives only +0.12/+0.35 mL for PE-to-DCM substitution, weakening a large general injection-solvent correction motivated by the different m92 EA-to-PE contrast. Persistent weak predicted dose sensitivity supports pausing further loading grids. Only observed records establish these outcomes. Adapted candidate predictions remain prospective questions; adaptive residuals and training-input fit do not estimate overall Row accuracy or establish retraining improvement. V2 minus V1 is elution interval width, and predictive quantile widths are not treated as calibrated uncertainty.
batch_rationale: The largest new failures were prospective transfer failures, especially pyridyl ketone, and incorrect solvent-response continuations. This batch combines connected nitrogen and oxygenated response tests with selected interpolation checks. The acid and m194 experiments address specific completion ambiguities that ordinary monotonicity assumptions cannot resolve. Naphthyl extensions test suspicious interval shapes without declaring predictions erroneous in advance. New cyclic ketone, diaryl ketone, aldehyde, benzoate, ether-acrylate and haloarene labels provide complementary support in ordinary Row chemistry. Their value is transferable coverage and interpretable contrasts, independent of acquisition-score magnitude.

possible_model_blind_spots: GENERAL CHEMICAL KNOWLEDGE: Increasing EA usually strengthens normal-phase elution. Pyridine-like nitrogen, sulfoxide oxygen and accessible hydroxyls can interact strongly with silica. Conjugation, steric accessibility and possible intramolecular hydrogen bonding can modify interactions. These priors motivate comparisons but do not explain the trajectory's unusual labels by themselves.

UNTESTED HYPOTHESES: Weak molecule-by-condition interactions, adsorption accessibility, dissolution and injection effects contribute to discrepancies. Shared TPSA and HBD/HBA totals cannot uniquely encode these distinctions.

Conflicting or unusual anchors may produce artificial response extrema or interval compression. The failed m73 near-repeat makes this concern concrete without identifying the cause of any unmeasured curve.
Completion-specific failure can coexist with reasonable onset prediction, as m194 showed historically. A common endpoint offset would miss that error structure.
chemistry_memo.coverage_or_redundancy_concerns: Distinct eligible IDs frequently encode identical complete physical inputs, including observed inputs. Replication is informative when tied to a specific ambiguity; catalog multiplicity and tiny density-derived mass differences do not independently add chemical coverage. Ordinary aromatic, ester, ketone and aldehyde conditions remain relevant to the Row objective alongside difficult polar graphs.

ml_memo.possible_model_blind_spots: INFERENCES: Severe errors include retention-level, solvent-slope and interval-width failures; a single bias correction would mix distinct problems. Sparse measured ratios can leave a molecule poorly covered even when similarity is 1. ML AND CHEMICAL PRIORS: Local smoothness, structural transfer, adsorption accessibility and injection effects motivate comparisons, but none independently establishes candidate truth or the mechanisms behind unusual records. The m73 conflict especially cautions against propagating one anomalous anchor across related graphs.
ml_memo.possible_learning_bottlenecks: Persistent flat loading responses suggest weak condition-feature use, inadequate scaling or insufficient graph-by-condition interactions; the packet does not identify the cause. More loading triplets may have low marginal value until existing differences can be expressed.
